attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter, said in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition matches his words, including 'basically'. It is a firm present-tense claim with no hedge, so it is an observation.

contract.note: He names no measure. Reading 'obvious use case' as a use that large-scale data plainly shows is an ordinary reading, and 'basically' leaves room for minor exceptions. Reading it as clear-ROI uses would be another option, but the usage reading is not stretched.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own data on itself, for one provider. Coding leads API traffic, but the same report shows sizeable non-coding use and puts coding at about 36% of Claude.ai. It does not show other uses as marginal.

Representative ChatGPT sample through July 2025. Practical guidance, information seeking and writing make up nearly 80% of conversations, writing leads work use, and programming is a small share. That shows other uses are plainly evident.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's plain reading, the largest LLM consumer product in mid-2025 was used mainly for non-coding tasks, with writing leading work use and coding a small share. That meets the contradiction condition. Anthropic's data shows coding leads for one provider's API, but it does not make other uses marginal. So coding was not 'basically the only' obvious use.

attribution.note: Zitron gives this as his own theory, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both 'my theory' and 'likely'. It is a speculative causal explanation: developers can't limit use, likely because of the architecture.

contract.note: Not scoring it is fair. He offers the sentence as a theory with a hedged cause, and 'no real way of limiting' has no threshold.

evidence.note: Shows Anthropic announced token-based weekly limits in July 2025. This bears on the premise, but it does not test whether the limits worked or what caused any failure.

reviews.rationale: He labels it his theory and hedges the cause with 'likely'. Under policy, a hedged speculative causal claim is not scored, and the architectural cause cannot be checked from outside the companies.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence. He paraphrases Brown for one sub-point but adopts it as his own.

semantics.note: It is a causal claim with an explicit 'because', and the proposition keeps his definition and reasons faithfully.

contract.note: The language is firm, but 'do software engineering', 'learn' and 'adapt' have no stated threshold or meaning. Any test chosen would decide the result. Not scoring it is fair.

evidence.note: Shows performance degrading with input length on simple non-code tasks. Consistent with the sub-claim, but it does not test the main claim.
Early 2025: models reliably completed only short software tasks, and the capability was growing fast. It does not test his definition.

reviews.rationale: This is a capability judgment resting on his own definition of software engineering, with undefined terms and no threshold. The evidence is context on the sub-claim about context length only. It is too vague to score, which is not a broken case.

attribution.note: Zitron reports what unnamed sources told him and endorses it ('sources also confirm').

semantics.note: A firm factual claim that utilization is about 60%. Leaving out the sourcing phrase does not change what he commits to.

contract.note: The plain reading (about 60% utilization around Aug–Sep 2025) is ordinary and fair. The 55–65% band suits 'barely scratching'.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evidence items. Microsoft publishes no Copilot GPU utilization figure, the only source for 60% is his anonymous sources, and the one contrary claim found was rejected as unreliable. The question was checked, and the available evidence does not settle it.
